cohort: The study included 126 women with singleton pregnancy (23-33 weeks' gestation) reporting signs and symptoms indicative of preterm labour.
finding: QfFN thresholds are a useful tool to distinguish pregnant women for PTB prediction risk <34 weeks' gestation, with increasing sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value as qfFN thresholds increase.
followup_time: Until 34 weeks' gestation or within 14 days from testing, depending on the specific outcome evaluated.
cross-section timing: When women with singleton pregnancy (23-33 weeks' gestation) reported signs and symptoms indicative of preterm labour.
gest_age: 23-33 weeks' gestation at testing, with an outcome definition of preterm birth <34 weeks' gestation.
